recognize_zh: 周邊血中一顆中性球只有兩個大塊狀、染色質粗凝的核葉，以細絲相連（pince-nez 樣的雙葉核），胞質顆粒大致保留；在晚期 HIV 病人，這種假性 Pelger 核低分葉屬於後天性的發育異常變化。
features: Neutrophil with a bilobed nucleus whose two lobes are connected by a thin chromatin filament (pince-nez configuration)
Lobes are large and somewhat irregular with coarsely clumped chromatin
Pale pink cytoplasm with preserved fine neutrophilic granules
Background red cells with mild anisocytosis and rouleaux-like stacking
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a neutrophil with a hyposegmented, bilobed nucleus in which two coarsely clumped lobes are joined by a thin filament, producing a pseudo-Pelger (pince-nez) appearance. The cytoplasm retains fine specific granules without obvious hypogranulation in this cell. Red cells show mild anisocytosis. In a patient with advanced HIV infection, this acquired pseudo-Pelger-Huet change is consistent with HIV-related myelodysplastic change, though a primary myelodysplastic neoplasm and drug effect should be considered clinically.

ddx.vs: Affects nearly all neutrophils uniformly with normal granulation in an asymptomatic person, whereas acquired changes are variable and accompany cytopenias or other dysplasia.
Also shows pseudo-Pelger cells, often with hypogranulation, but requires persistent cytopenias, multilineage dysplasia and/or clonal genetic abnormalities without a reversible cause.

ddx.dx: Drug-induced pseudo-Pelger change (e.g. mycophenolate, valproate, taxanes)
ddx.vs: Morphologically identical; distinguished by medication history and resolution after withdrawal.
Has a curved, non-segmented band of uniform width without two discrete lobes joined by a filament.
